territorial_scope.description: Extends to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

summary.short: Sets the £250 million threshold figure for qualifying worldwide revenue, at or above which providers of regulated services must notify OFCOM and pay fees under sections 83 and 84 of the Online Safety Act 2023, from the charging year beginning 1 April 2026.
summary.long: Made under section 86(2) of the Online Safety Act 2023 as the first regulations under section 86, and in force from 11 December 2025 in England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. Regulation 2(1) specifies a threshold figure of £250 million for the purposes of section 83 (duty to notify OFCOM) and section 84 (duty to pay fees). Regulation 2(2) provides that the figure takes effect from the beginning of the charging year beginning 1 April 2026. The explanatory note (not part of the Regulations) states that providers whose qualifying worldwide revenue is at or above the figure must notify OFCOM unless they meet an exemption published by OFCOM and approved by the Secretary of State, and that OFCOM's fees are determined by reference to qualifying worldwide revenue for the qualifying period as defined in S.I. 2025/1032. It also notes that the initial notification falls within four months of the Regulations coming into force. The instrument contains no sanctions and no other thresholds. The figure follows an OFCOM consultation and advice, and the Secretary of State must keep it under review under section 86(3).

thresholds.consequence: Providers at or above the threshold figure have a duty to notify OFCOM (s.83) and to pay fees (s.84) of the Online Safety Act 2023, unless exempt.
thresholds.conditions: Provider is not exempt from the duties to notify and pay fees under sections 83 and 84 (Explanatory Note: exemptions published by OFCOM and approved by the Secretary of State, s.83(6)). The figure takes effect from the beginning of the charging year beginning 1 April 2026 (reg. 2(2)).

obligations.note: The operative provisions (regulation 1 and regulation 2) set the threshold figure and its commencement for the purposes of sections 83 and 84 of the Online Safety Act 2023. The duties to notify OFCOM and to pay fees are imposed by those sections of the Act, not by this instrument, so no obligations are coded here. The threshold is recorded under thresholds, not obligations.

enforcement.note: The instrument only specifies a threshold figure (reg. 2) under s.86 of the Online Safety Act 2023. It states no fines, penalties, licence revocation, suspension, blocking or other sanctions. It refers to the duties to notify (s.83) and pay fees (s.84) but does not state any consequence of breaching them.
